blocks.title: Fossil fuels
blocks.text: Petroleum (crude oil), coal and natural gas are collectively called fossil fuels.

Crude oil is extracted from underground reservoirs and refined in large plants by fractional distillation. The major products from petroleum are naphtha, gasoline, kerosene and diesel. Methane (CH4) is the major component of natural gas, mixed with ethane, propane and butane; it is used mainly to make ammonia (for fertilisers) and methanol (for solvents and fuel). Coal is not as useful as it once was, but it is still a petrochemical raw material where reserves are large. Its primary use here is to obtain benzene, toluene and xylene, which are vital in the manufacture of dyes, resins and explosives.

blocks.title: Keep in mind
blocks.text: Although fossil fuels are highly efficient sources of energy, burning them produces greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide (CO2). This leads to air pollution, global warming and climate change.
